# SK7051 — A suppression attribute has no justification

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`SuppressMessage` or `UnconditionalSuppressMessage` omits a meaningful `Justification`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A suppression attribute survives refactoring and is easy to read past, so its reason is part of the code review record. A nonempty `Justification` tells a future reader which analyzer assumption does not hold and whether the exception can be retired. The tool reports the omission but cannot write the explanation on the author's behalf.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
[SuppressMessage("Design", "CA1024")]
```

Write:

```csharp
[SuppressMessage("Design", "CA1024", Justification = "Reads the filesystem.")]
```

## When it does not fire

Only attributes semantically resolved to the framework suppression types are inspected, so a user attribute with the same short name is ignored. Empty strings and TODO/FIXME/TBD/N/A placeholders are not treated as reasons; the rule cannot assess otherwise substantive-looking prose.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7051.severity`
